causes.text: Great Wall Motor's chairman warned that China's electric-vehicle sector had entered an unhealthy price war, saying industry players were caught in a race to the bottom and urging companies to stop the discounting spiral to avoid long-term damage.

source_info.title: EV price war draws criticism from Great Wall Motor as discounts deepen

effects.text: One month later, BYD cut production shifts and delayed planned capacity expansions at its Shenzhen and Xi'an factories, citing the need to reduce inventory levels and protect margins as China's EV price war eroded profitability.

source_info.title: BYD cuts production shifts and delays capacity expansion as price war bites

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Great Wall Motor's chairman publicly criticized the EV price war, highlighting unsustainable discounting and warning peers to stop racing to the bottom.
The comments signaled industry-wide concern that deepening price cuts were eroding profitability and inventory health across Chinese EV makers.
A month later, BYD reduced production shifts and delayed capacity expansions at key factories, citing the need to control inventory and protect margins amid the ongoing price war.
Investors anticipated slower growth and margin pressure following the production curbs, the stock price fell 3.39% next day.

rationale: Great Wall Motor's warning exemplified growing alarm within China's EV sector over unsustainable discounting. BYD's subsequent decision to scale back production and delay expansion suggests a causal link: the escalating price war and public calls for restraint pressured the company to prioritize profitability over volume growth.
counterfactual_analysis: If industry peers had not spoken out against the price war, BYD might have maintained its planned production ramp-up rather than cutting shifts and delaying expansions.

adversarial_confounders.impact: BYD could have reduced production because of seasonal sales fluctuations rather than competitor criticism.

details.commentary: New EV brands and smart-car platforms offered Chinese consumers alternatives to traditional foreign marques. As these substitutes gained traction, established players like Mercedes-Benz faced growing pressure to localize and refresh their offerings to remain relevant.

details.pestel_factor: Technological - Shift toward smart, software-defined vehicles in China
details.commentary: Chinese buyers increasingly valued connected, software-rich vehicles that integrate seamlessly with local digital ecosystems. Mercedes-Benz's deeper partnerships with Chinese tech companies aimed to adapt to this technological shift, but also underlined how quickly the competitive landscape was evolving.
